comparisons.comparison: Both BAC and Morgan Stanley disclose credit loss provisions for their commercial lending portfolios in 2024, identifying corporate loan growth as a primary driver for increased provisions. BAC specifically notes that its Non-U.S. commercial loan portfolio grew by $12.9 billion (10%) driven by Global Markets, while MS attributes its $202 million provision primarily to 'growth in the corporate loan portfolio' alongside specific commercial real estate provisions. Both highlight credit risk management within the broader commercial/corporate lending business lines, though BAC provides specific geographic segmentation (Non-U.S.) and segment breakdowns (Global Banking vs. Markets), whereas MS aggregates the driver at the portfolio level.
